newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai oil firms up retail prices after baht float.
newsitem.headline: Thai oil firms up retail prices after baht float.

text.p: Major foreign oil companies in Thailand raised pump prices on Friday to reflect higher costs prompted by de facto devaluation of the baht last week.
Caltex, Shell and Esso raised their retail prices by around 18 satangs per litre across the board, industry sources told Reuters.
Retail diesel and petrol prices in June were around 8.30 and 9.51 baht a litre respectively.
"We are closely observing the government's request that the hike be done in stages to minimise effects on consumers," an official at Caltex Oil Thailand said.
"But we do not have details yet on when the prices will be adjusted again."
Other retail leaders, like the state-run Petroleum Authority of Thailand and Bangkchak Petroleum Plc, did not raise prices but said they might do so this weekend.
The baht has depreciated by around 15-20 percent since it was released from a peg to a basket of currencies dominated by the dollar into a managed float system on July 2.
Oil industry sources said the oil price hike was inevitable given the weaker baht and rising production costs.
They estimated that if the baht stayed around 28.00-29.00 to the dollar, retail oil prices would be 25-50 satangs per litre higher.
But the government, which has pledged not to intervene to cap the oil prices, has asked oil companies to pass the extra cost on to the public in stages.
The effect of the baht float seemed to be spreading on Friday. Immediately after oil prices rose, some wholesalers said they too would start raising prices to reflect higher costs.
"If the transportation and production costs rise, we have no choice but to pass it to retail stores," said Vilai Kowviratanachai, a wholesale clothes distributor in Bangkok.
The commerce ministry, however, vowed it would be tough on profiteering and hoarding to keep prices under control.
